reference: An external reference implemented in Python along three routes that never read the tool's arithmetic. (1) First principles: one-dimensional isentropic nozzle flow parametrised by throat Mach number, the mass flux assembled as rho*w and the choking point located numerically by maximising that flux, verified against NACA Report 1135 Table I at M=1, k=1.4 (p/p0 = 0.528282, T/T0 = 0.833333, rho/rho0 = 0.633938) to better than 4e-7. (2) The published sizing equations themselves, implemented from the standards' own stated algebraic form and their own printed constants in their own units: API Standard 520 Part I, 9th ed. (2014), clause 5.6.3 (critical vapour, C = 520 sqrt(k(2/(k+1))^((k+1)/(k-1))) US customary and 0.03948 sqrt(...) SI), clause 5.6.4 (subcritical vapour, 735 and 17.9, with F2) and clause 5.8.1.2 (liquid, 38 and 11.78); and ISO 4126-1:2013 clause 7.3.3.1 (critical vapour, C = 3.948 sqrt(...)). The API and ISO coefficient tables are reproduced from these forms (C = 315, 337, 356, 373, 387, 400 at k = 1.0 to 2.0; ISO C = 2.703 at k = 1.4). (3) Real-gas choked flux from the CoolProp multiparameter equations of state, used to measure what the tool's declared ideal-gas idealisation costs. The three routes are cross-checked against each other before any tool output is graded. The 49 in-page algebraic identities from the previous artifact are merged and kept, labelled self-check, and counted separately.

provenance_note: Written independently in Python for this benchmark. The page's JavaScript was read only for input names, units, defaults, the declared phase switch, the declared model boundary and the list of reported quantities; nothing was transcribed, ported or paraphrased from it, and no reference route evaluates any expression taken from it. The reference was self-verified before any tool output was graded: NACA TR-1135 Table I reproduced to 4e-7; the numerically located choking point matched to the closed form of Shapiro eq. 4.19 over k = 1.05 to 1.8; branch continuity and flux stationarity checked at the transition; the limits k -> 1, Z -> 1, back pressure -> 0 and back pressure -> upstream checked; the API 520 and ISO 4126-1 published coefficient tables reproduced; and each standard's printed constant compared with the exact unit-consistent constant it rounds. Grading tolerances are read off that last comparison, i.e. off each standard's own stated numerical precision, never off what the tool produces. A negative control was run before publication: three deliberately falsified expectations produced exactly the corresponding failures and moved nothing else. Run by bench-src/gen_relief_valve_sizing.py. Of the 347 graded checks, 245 are recomputed -- by that reference, or, for the retained in-page identities, by the tool itself -- and 102 are graded against the published, rounded sizing coefficients of API 520 Part I and ISO 4126-1 reused as those standards print them, each to a tolerance read off that rounding and reported in published_constant_rounding.
tolerance: Each tolerance comes from the physics or from the standard's own printed precision. First-principles routes: 1e-12 relative, the double-precision path difference between two arithmetic assemblies of the same exact solution. API 520 clause 5.6.3 critical: 5.0e-5 SI and 2.5e-3 US customary, from the rounding of the published constants 0.03948 and 520 against the exact 0.0394807513 and 519.4483 that isentropic flow implies (1.903e-5 and 1.062e-3). ISO 4126-1 clause 7.3.3.1: 5.0e-5, from 3.948 against 3.948075127 (1.903e-5). API 520 clause 5.6.4 subcritical: 1.5e-3, from 17.9 against 17.9101653 (5.676e-4) and 735 against 734.6096 (5.316e-4). API 520 clause 5.8.1.2 liquid: 2.0e-4 SI and 6.0e-4 US customary, from 11.78 against 11.779218 (6.64e-5) and 38 against 37.99242 (1.99e-4). Regime classification and the declared-boundary refusal are categorical. The merged in-page self-checks keep the page's own 1e-12 identity figure. No code-compliance tolerance is claimed and no result here is a compliance statement.
scope: This artifact records how far the tool's preliminary relief area sits from the published API 520 Part I and ISO 4126-1 sizing equations and from first-principles compressible nozzle flow, across the tool's declared input range. It is not a compliance assessment. The comparison is only possible with every correction factor the tool declares it does not implement - Kb, Kc, Kw, Kv - set to unity, and with the discharge coefficient the user types used in place of a certified Kd; an area produced by this tool is not a certified effective orifice area and is not a valve selection. API 520/521 or ISO 4126 compliance and certified-valve corrections are not claimed.
grading: total counts graded checks. 298 are independent checks against the external reference described above, spread over 41 driven cases. 49 are the in-page algebraic identities carried forward from the previous artifact and merged here; they are labelled kind="self-check" on every row and are NOT evidence of agreement with anything outside the tool. Every row carries kind, route and tolerance_basis so any verdict can be re-derived. The real-gas rows are measurements of the declared model boundary and carry no acceptance criterion, so they are excluded from the count.
headline: Across the whole driven range the tool's gas core is the exact one-dimensional isentropic nozzle solution and its liquid core is the exact incompressible Bernoulli solution: both agree with the first-principles route to floating-point precision. Against the published sizing equations the agreement is limited only by the rounding of each standard's own printed constant - 1.9e-5 for API 520 SI critical and ISO 4126-1, 1.1e-3 for API 520 US customary critical, 5.7e-4 for API 520 subcritical and 6.6e-5 to 2.0e-4 for the API liquid clause. No divergence of substance was found anywhere in the range. What the tool does not have is the standards' correction factors, and that gap is structural and already declared, not numerical.

As k -> 1 the critical ratio tends to exp(-1/2) = 0.606531 (expand (k/(k-1)) ln(2/(k+1)) about k=1).
Constant Z enters only as R_eff = Z R, so G scales exactly as Z^(-1/2).  Z=4 must halve the flux.
Below the critical ratio the flux is independent of back pressure; discharging to 1 Pa must give the same flux as to 1 bar.
As r -> 1 the flux must vanish.  At 1-r = 1e-9 it is 6.5e-5 of the choked value, so the check is that it has collapsed by more than four decades.

Expanding r^(2/k) - r^((k+1)/k) about r = 1 gives (1-r)(k-1)/k, so G -> p1 sqrt(2 (1-r)/(R_eff T)) independently of k.  The next term is O(1-r) = 1e-9 relative, so 1e-6 is three decades of headroom on the asymptote itself.

not_benchmarked: Certified Kd and the API 520/521 and ISO 4126 correction factors for back pressure (Kb, Kw), rupture disc combination (Kc) and viscosity (Kv). The tool implements none of them, so every comparison here is made at Kb = Kc = Kw = Kv = 1. Where a real installation carries Kb < 1, the standards' required area exceeds the tool's by exactly 1/Kb; that factor is a device correction, not physics, and no value for it is asserted here.

The 1.25 p overpressure convention of the API liquid clause. The tool is handed a differential pressure directly and makes no overpressure claim, so the liquid clause is evaluated at the actual differential.

ISO 4126-1 subcritical compressible flow. The critical clause is implemented and verified against the standard's own tabulated C; the subcritical clause is not, so no ISO comparison is recorded on subcritical cases.

notes: Independent cases are driven through the shipping page in a real browser by permalink, and the page's own calculation record is read back. The reference is evaluated separately in Python and the two are compared; the page is never asked to check itself on any row labelled independent.
Every independent row names its route and the clause or equation it came from, and its tolerance_basis states where the tolerance came from.

The in-page self-checks are reproduced by calling window.__dgcBenchmark() on the tool and are merged here unchanged apart from the kind, route and tolerance_basis labels that mark them as self-checks.

Real-gas rows measure the cost of the declared ideal-gas, constant-Z, constant-k idealisation against multiparameter equations of state, with the ideal route fed the EOS's own local Z and k so that only the VARIATION of Z and k along the expansion remains. The departure is 0.05 % for air at 1.5 bar and 0.01 % at 11 bar, and grows with reduced pressure and with proximity to the critical point: 0.64 % for air at 50 bar, 1.5 % at 200 bar; 2.2 % for methane at 50 bar / 320 K and 3.6 % at 150 bar; 3.2 % for hydrogen at 200 bar; and 12.3 % for carbon dioxide at 60 bar / 330 K, a reduced temperature of 1.09. That last case is the sharpest result in this artifact and its SIGN matters: the ideal flux exceeds the real one, so the idealisation over-states what the device can pass and therefore UNDER-states the area required. The page prints its area to 0.1 mm2, about 2e-4 relative on a typical result, so the idealisation exceeds the tool's own printed precision from roughly a reduced pressure of 0.04 upward - which is most real relief service. This is not a defect of the tool, which declares the idealisation openly; it is the measured size of the declared model boundary, and it is why the tool is a screen and not a sizing authority.
